Subject: Deployment mode selection — next steps & pricing options

Hi Priya / Samir,

Thanks again for taking the time today — really helpful to understand Aperture's goals for moving your summarization and search assistants off the on-prem GPU cluster. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have alignment: 

- Current state: self-hosted GPU cluster (Nvidia A100, mixed infra) running a fine-tuned model. Peak inference ~120 qps, typical 25–40 qps.
- Main goals: reduce ops overhead, improve tail latency, and ensure predictable unit costs; must preserve PII controls and SOC 2 evidence for contracts.
- Deployment modes we discussed: Hosted API (fastest to ship), Dedicated capacity (predictable throughput + data isolation), Private VPC / on-prem package (required if strict network isolation / procurement).

Proposed next steps:
1) Neha to provide a migration playbook and initial technical checklist (network, egress, data flows).
2) Connor / infra to size Dedicated config and provide cost estimate based on peak qps and average token length.
3) Marissa to send draft commercial (pricing tiers + SOW) and confirm procurement timeline.
4) Schedule 60-minute technical deep-dive next week (ops + security).

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-pricing.pdf (pricing tiers) — please see the Dedicated vs Private pricing table on page 2.

Quick question for you both: is data residency a hard requirement (EU/US)? Also any mandated certs beyond SOC 2 (e.g., FedRAMP, HIPAA)?

Thanks — I’ll coordinate calendar options after we get the technical checklist.

Best,
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side after sync with infra and procurement: 

- Residency/certs: data must remain in US regions for now. We are HIPAA-sensitive in one product line (customer PII) but do not yet require FedRAMP. SOC 2 + BAAs will be required for the HIPAA scope.
- Timeline: Procurement wants an out-the-door vendor agreement within 6–8 weeks.
- Migration constraints: our current on-prem cluster has some custom batching logic and a bespoke KV cache; we want minimal feature regression (latency and response quality must be equal or better).
- Cost sensitivity: we are evaluating total cost of ownership; dedicated reserved pricing preferred if it lowers monthly spend over sustained usage.

Two asks before the technical call:
1) Can you share a migration checklist that outlines required logs/artifacts we need to export (e.g., model weights not allowed, but inference traces/throughput logs etc.)?
2) Ballpark run-rate for Dedicated that would cover peak 120 qps with 99th percentile latency target of <200ms (we're happy to provide average token lengths).

Samir and I are available Wed/Thu next week in the afternoon.

Thanks,
Priya
Head of Infrastructure, Aperture Retail
priya.rao@apertureretail.com

Hi Priya / Samir — thanks for the notes and the constraints. Couple quick technical answers and I attached a draft migration playbook (migration-playbook-v1.docx):

1) Residency & compliance: we support US-only deployment for both Dedicated and Private VPC. We can also provide a BAA and SOC 2 artifact bundle for the HIPAA-scoped product. For Private/on-prem, you keep keys and control the network.

2) Migration checklist (high level):
   - Provide inference traces (timestamped requests, token counts, latency) for a 72-hour window that includes a peak.
   - Sample prompts + expected outputs for our evals (to check for regressions).
   - KV/cache semantics docs (how your cache keys are computed, TTLs) — we map to Redwood’s KV caching and can preserve semantics in most cases.
   - Network egress rules & firewall IPs for initial provisioning.

3) Dedicated sizing ballpark: given 120 qps peak and target 99p <200ms (including network), we estimate two reserved 8xA100-equivalent units with autoscaling headroom for bursts. Ballpark monthly run-rate for a committed Dedicated pool (monthly reserved) is ~$55k–80k depending on token churn and model size. Hosted API is cheaper TTV but not appropriate if you need strict isolation or BAAs. Private VPC / on-prem is higher up-front (integration + infra) but removes network egress and meets the strictest compliance needs.

4) Operational notes: we have a migration utilities repo that can replay traces into a staging Dedicated pool to validate latency and throughput before cutover. If you can share a 72-hour trace file (anonymized), we’ll run a replay test.

I attached the migration playbook and included a short checklist on page 3. Connor / Dylan — can you confirm expected ingress IP ranges and any specific auth flows we should support for Aperture’s SSO?

Cheers,
Neha Kapoor
